c1a.text: The nose stands out from the face.

correction.truth: The nose is carved: it projects from the smooth face.

c1b.text: Yes. The nose is cut from the same block and stands out from the face. Everything else was painted.

correction.truth: The nose is carved from the marble; the record lists no other material.

c1m.text: Carved nose, painted eyes: two techniques on one face.

c2a.text: No paint shows here: it is broken stone.

correction.tempting: The patch differs in tone from the rest.
correction.truth: It is a chip: a piece of the cheek has broken off.
The record notes a chip on the left cheek: the stone has broken.

c2c.text: Yes. The Louvre records a chip on the head's left cheek, which is on our right as we face it.

c2m.text: A small chip in a smooth face.

c3a.text: Yes. The record says the base of the neck has been completed. It does not say when, or with what.

c3b.text: The body is lost: no shoulders survive.

correction.tempting: It sits where shoulders would begin.
correction.truth: The record says the base of the neck was completed later.

c3c.text: The stand is below, in dark grey.

correction.truth: This piece is the neck's base, completed later; the mount is underneath.

c3m.text: The base of the neck: a later completion.

regionSources.title: Dayton Art Institute, 'Female Figure' (Cycladic, Spedos type), with a Smarthistory transcript
regionSources.quote: Look at the shield-like shape of the face and the way that the nose projects. They’re beautiful without eyes but there were painted eyes.
regionSources.supports: On such faces the nose is carved and projects; the eyes were painted.

regionSources.title: Museum of Cycladic Art, Athens, 'Exhibition Topics' (Cycladic Society 5,000 Years Ago)
regionSources.quote: Cycladic figurines were originally painted. Deep blue or black pigment was used for the hair, eyebrows, eyes, and pubic triangle
regionSources.supports: Features such as eyes and brows were painted, not carved.

regionSources.supports: Our translation: material: marble; technique: carved in the round. One block of marble, no other material recorded.
